title: Proactive Warm Gatekeeper and Tenant-aware Primer for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a "Proactive Warm Gatekeeper" subsystem that makes admission decisions for prewarming dedicated nodes. The gatekeeper will accept tenant-level policies (throughput guarantees, cost budget, cold-start sensitivity) and coordinate: (1) staged model weight loading (partial vs full), (2) KV cache priming strategies (prefix-only, selective embeddings, synthetic seeds), and (3) autoscaler hints and budgeted prewarm reservations. The goal is to reduce 95th/99th percentile cold-start latency for provisioned capacity while keeping prewarm cost within configurable budgets and preserving SLA-backed throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gatekeeper API implemented and documented; 2) Supports policy-driven prewarm decisions per-tenant; 3) Demonstrated reduction in p95 cold-start token latency by >=40% for targeted workloads in lab benchmark; 4) Prewarm budget enforcement prevents >5% overrun in a 24h noisy workload test; 5) Telemetry exposes prewarm admission, success/fail, KV priming hit-rate, weight-load duration, and cost estimate for each admission; 6) Rollout plan and canary strategy defined for dedicated fleets.
technical_notes:
- Admission heuristics: demand forecasting (60s and 5m windows), tenant SLA tier, recent request spike detector, and model residency fingerprints.
- Weight loading modes: quick-index (top layers + kv-index), staged-stream (progressive weight stream to avoid blocking), and full-load.
- KV priming modes: prefix-only (common prompt prefixes), sample-seed (sampled recent requests), and synthetic-backfill (LLM-generated candidate prefixes).
- Autoscaler integration: gatekeeper publishes transient reservations and env hints to the autoscaler to avoid prewarm throttling.
- Safety: prewarm jobs run with ephemeral limits; failed prewarm triggers rollback and circuit-breaker to avoid cascading budget burns.
- Telemetry: add metrics warm_gatekeeper.admissions, warm_gatekeeper.failures, warm_gatekeeper.kv_hit_rate, weight_load.duration_ms (histogram), prewarm.cost_estimate_usd.
implementation_plan: 1) Spike (2d): implement a prototype gatekeeper service and simple admission rules; 2) Lab test (4d): run against synthetic traffic generator with models of different sizes; 3) Integrate autoscaler hints (3d); 4) Add KV priming strategies and telemetry (4d); 5) Internal canary on single dedicated pool with conservative budget (2 weeks); 6) Gradual rollout with monitoring and rollback playbook.
risks:
- Over-aggressive prewarming may increase unit cost and steal capacity from live traffic.
- Incorrect demand forecasting leads to missed spikes or wasted prewarm.
- KV priming that uses synthetic seeds could bias model outputs if used for evaluation datasets.
- Edge cases: tenant churn and model swaps causing stale prewarm snapshots.
rollout_steps:
- Merge feature branch behind a feature flag.
- Enable telemetry and budget alerts.
- Canary: 1 dedicated pool (low traffic) for 48h.
- Observe metrics and tune heuristics.
- Gradually increase pools and tenant coverage over 2 weeks.
- Post-mortem after full rollout.
metrics_and_observability: Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 cold-start latency, prewarm.admit_rate, prewarm.success_rate, prewarm.budget_used_pct, kv.primed_hit_rate. Dashboards: per-tenant time-series and per-model aggregates. Alerts: prewarm.budget_used_pct > 80% for 1h, prewarm.success_rate < 95% for 15m, p95 cold-start latency increases by >20% vs baseline.
qa_checks:
- Unit tests for admission rules.
- E2E lab run with synthetic traffic covering sudden spikes and slow ramps.
- Chaos test: induce weight-load failures and verify circuit-breaker behavior.
- Cost test: run 24h noisy workload and verify budget enforcement.
- Security review of any agent that fetches private weights (KMS/HSM integration).
